final_truth: Guernica* (1937) by Pablo Picasso is a powerful anti-war statement. Created in response to the bombing of the Basque town during the Spanish Civil War, the black-and-white mural depicts suffering, chaos, and fear through distorted figures and symbolic imagery. A bull and a horse dominate the scene, representing strength and terror. This masterpiece remains one of the most enduring symbols of the horrors of war.
